

## **Panel A: Unreported second (liens by same lender)**

Low/No-Doc

Best:  $\beta=-2.0\%$ ;  $t$ -statistic= $-4.65$   
Worst:  $\beta=2.7\%$ ;  $t$ -statistic= $1.74$

Full-Doc

Best:  $\beta=0.9\%$ ;  $t$ -statistic= $0.98$   
Worst:  $\beta=14.8\%$ ;  $t$ -statistic= $6.84$

The figure consists of two side-by-side plots. The left plot, titled 'Low/No-Doc', shows the probability of an unreported second (y-axis, 0 to 0.5) against the credit score (x-axis, 540 to 780). Data points are represented by grey triangles and black circles. A blue dashed line and a yellow dashed line show the best and worst fits, respectively. The right plot, titled 'Full-Doc', shows the same variables. It includes a red solid line for the best fit and a black solid line for the worst fit. Both plots show a general increase in probability with credit score, peaking around 660-700.

Two scatter plots showing the probability of an unreported second against credit score. The left panel (Low/No-Doc) shows a relatively flat trend with a best and worst beta of 0.5%. The right panel (Full-Doc) shows a more complex trend with a best beta of 3.3% and a worst beta of -0.5%. Both panels include several fitted lines (solid, dashed, blue) and a horizontal reference line at 0.10.
